title.narrative: Enhancing Access to Finance and Markets for MSMEs

description.narrative: While closing down ongoing MSME support initiative in the intermediate FY period, the project envisages a phased approach to developing a new cross-Secretariat project to deliver this outcome under three key high-level outputs in the 2025/26 fiscal year:1. Project development – this includes: a. Establishment of a cross-Secretariat project team under the sponsorship of a senior leader, and with members drawn from EDTI, SDYG and Communications, a terms of reference for the project and clear delivery and reporting lines. b. Research and analysis to determine the gaps in MSME access to finance and participation across the Commonwealth, with particular attention to gender inequality and youth exclusion. This exercise will also identify initial pilot countries/regions as well as potential delivery partners and funders. c. Formulation of a draft project with an articulated theory of change, analysis of risk, public communications and a strategy for mobilising resources to deliver the project. 2. Partnership establishment – this includes: a. Dialogue with Commonwealth Accredited Organisations active in representing MSMEs and other relevant sectors; b. Dialogue with multilateral partners and peak bodies representing MSMEs; c. Formalisation of any key relationships that will be engaged in delivering the project where needed. 3. Consultation – this includes a. Consultation with member countries to identify initial pilot countries/regions. This may be done through the Secretariat’s existing forums – e.g. the Finance Ministers Meeting, the Consultation of National Women’s Machineries, briefings to the Board of Governors b. Internal consultation to ensure consistency with the Secretariat’s operational policy frameworks 4. Resource mobilisation – this will need to be considered simultaneously to partnership and consultation described above. Early attention is essential to ensure consistency with the Secretariat’s operational policies, and with the requirements of donors or other partners. A key focus will be on seeking to ensure harmonisation in the requirements of different partner groups. While MSMEs face myriad challenges in the global trade landscape, the newly framed Commonwealth MSME project will be differentiated to advance the Strategic objective of the SP and to focus on a narrow result bandwidth of market access, adoption of innovative digital technologies and greater access to finance while enagaging with partners and AOs to advance support in other areas of work
